Finley.feeling: Tense and murky: Finley died right after Alex's Mouser visit, and the table is pushing toward a vote on Alex.

Alex.note: Final round: throw every card I hold. Ellis has the most conflicting claims, so all eight cards go at Ellis.

Blair.note: Consensus is Alex. I have no Wild left, so I throw my lowest card, C1, to keep the high cards.

Casey.note: Alex is the strongest Meowfia suspect, and Farm is ahead on the dead player's evidence. I'll throw three cards at Alex to secure the vote while keeping my higher cards.

Drew.note: Alex is the strongest read: the Mouser visit on Finley and the collapse right after. I'll throw my lowest real card at Alex.

Ellis.note: Alex is the strongest target after Finley's collapse following Alex's Mouser visit. I'll throw one low card, D4, to keep my higher cards.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still scores. Alex is the one the table suspects, so I'll throw my lowest card at Alex to limit the risk.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's dawn gain was hard to read: Finley's +1 was reported, but the table couldn't tell whose visit caused it, so it fed a lot of suspicion. Confirming whether a Wink-visited or Eagle-visited egg counts as a visit would help.
Alex.fun: Going all-in with all eight cards in the final round banked 65 points for Meowfia, which was the biggest swing of the game.
Alex.change: Make it clearer, in the dawn reports, exactly who visited whom, so players aren't guessing from egg counts alone.
Alex.regret: Winking Finley on day 3 made me look guilty after my Mouser visit, and it didn't gain much; I'd hold the Wink for a clearer target and avoid drawing that suspicion.

Blair.confusing: Eggsecution counts and card values were hard to read. Votes are counted by card, not by player, so a player who throws 8 cards can swing a round, and I couldn't tell how much of a threat that was until it happened.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Casey switched from Pigeon to Kookaburra and Ellis also claimed Kookaburra. The table pieced together who was lying from visit claims and egg counts, and it was a real puzzle.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports clearer when someone is confused, so players know which number to trust. My own confused report made my egg count nearly useless as evidence.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I voted with the table on Alex and threw only single low cards, so my throws barely mattered when Ellis took 8 votes. I should have checked Ellis's claimed roles against the Hawk result more directly and pushed harder on who was lying before the vote.

Casey.confusing: How a Turkey or Eagle gains eggs from visitors was hard to check, since the table couldn't see who visited whom and nest changes could come from several sources.
Casey.fun: Round 3's collapse of Finley right after Alex claimed a Mouser visit made the Meowfia read clear, and the table turned on Alex.
Casey.change: Tell players which visits caused each egg change, so role claims can be checked against the nest counts.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I first claimed Pigeon and then switched to Kookaburra after Drew challenged me, which made me look guilty and got me eggsecuted. I would stick with one consistent claim and defend it.

Drew.confusing: The Storyteller's rule that a Pigeon-turned-Kookaburra or two players claiming the same role can both be sincere made it hard to judge claims. The round 3 Eagle egg count also looked inconsistent until the visit mechanics were explained.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: Casey's role switches from Pigeon to Kookaburra to Tit-check exposed a liar, and the table converged on them. Casey was Sphinx, Meowfia, so the read was right.
Drew.change: Make the Storyteller's dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so visit claims can be checked without guessing. That would reduce the dispute over Eagle and Turkey counts.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw only one card at Alex, the real Mouser. I should have thrown more to make sure the vote went to Alex, since Alex's eight votes on Ellis decided the round.

Ellis.confusing: The Eggsecution scoring was hard to read: a single player can throw up to 8 cards, and the vote count alone does not show whether it is a bluff or real confidence. Also, a dead player's throw still counts for cards but not as a vote, which was easy to miss.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Casey kept switching roles under pressure, and the table worked it out from Kookaburra and Pigeon claims that could not both be true.
Ellis.change: I would make the day's special actions, like Wink, show more clearly what is known, since a collapse was the only clue in round 3 and was easy to misread.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I called CAW to end the day before Alex had properly answered the Mouser visit. I would have pressed Alex for a clear account first, then voted.

Finley.confusing: The Storyteller's counts of visitors and eggs were hard to reconcile, since a Hawk or Eagle gain could come from several sources. The Kookaburra confusion rule also made some claims impossible to verify.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was fun: my Turkey claim was challenged, and the table's vote on Alex turned out to be right, with Alex as the Sphinx.
Finley.change: I'd make the round-by-round role reveals and visit records easier to track, so players can check each other's claims without relying on memory.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw only one card at Alex, the Mouser, while Farm was losing the vote, so I'd have thrown more to push the vote harder and protect our side's count.
